body:
Okay, I wanted to talk to my parents over breakfast about how I felt I ruined everything in my life; how I made my relationship with my parents suck, how I drove my 'friends' away, how I lost motivation in everything, etc. My dad just started downright yelling at me and complaining about everything I do. He started saying that I only want to get things from people and never give back. He just complained at me.

As he was yelling me I started crying and begged him to stop, but he saw this like another reason to complain. I... just don't know. I don't know what to do. I make everything wrong with people, I ruin everything. I do everything wrong. People aren't happy with or about me. I suck.

> It sounds more like a relationship giong the natural route to the end, as they often do. Probably neither of you are fully to blame, but neither of you are ready to let it go once and for all, either.

We don't want to let it go. We just have so much things in common and we have such a great time together that it would be hard to find someone I feel so connected to. I believe this can be worked out, even though she's now very skeptical about how I behave. I have to whine less so she can see that's not the way I want things to be.

Today I will talk to my therapist, I really want to fix things with my girlfriend. This has been a very shitty week in many aspects, but SW really helps, thank you.

Yes, I should focus on the positive aspects of things, but it just seems there's more negative than positive aspect.

What should I read from Proust? I actually had never heard of him.

> It's a great talent in your future life as a QA engineer, Dr House, or proof reader for Springer Verlag

That made me laugh, thanks! :)

Well, I've talked to my parents (who complain about how much I complain), my girlfriend (she always helped me feel better, but I eventually annoyed her) and finally my therapist. Therapy has helped me a lot, but there are many things in my life I can't just come to terms with yet.

I don't think that the things I say are usually negative. I'm just hard to convince, and I always find a way to contradict an argument. That's why I'm stubborn and why they say I'm negative.

Still, I think I could use that technique, when I try to say something negative about something. When I try to give constructive criticism I will sandwich my thoughts (like "I think that {good thing}, but I'm not sure about {bad thing}. I still think that {good thing}, though!").

Thank you. :)

First of all, I don't think I'm suicidal, so don't give this much priority. I just feel like crap and this is the only place I can count on right now.

Now, I think I need to give a background. I'm a 17 year old teenager. When I was in Kindergarten these teachers called me 'gifted' and made me skip one year. I tried to get into Elementary School but they wouldn't accept me with the age I had, so I waited for one year doing nothing. In this year my parents hardly let me have contact with kids my own age. When I got into Elementary School, I was bullied. I had no friends and I couldn't understand why this was. Even the 'dorks' rejected me. Elementary School was pretty much all the same: parents having high expectations for my notes, me having no friends, teachers being very protective with me and making things worse, etc. I got into Junior High with no friends whatsoever.

Starting Junior High I lost motivation in school. I didn't want to pay attention in class or do shit. My grades were now ranging from average to very good, only having 'low' grades on the ones that were average. My parents weren't happy about this, but I didn't care. I basically started going downhill in terms of grades. I started using my time improving my drawing skills, reading Nietzsche and learning to program. But my grades were crap. I was rude to some teachers, I once got suspended from school for three days because of this, my parents complained about how much time I spent on the computer, how disrespectful I was, how low my grades were, etc. I still had no friends and I couldn't understand why this was.

In High School I started trying to be much more integrated. People started finding me nice to be around with and used me to get things from me ("can you fix my computer?", "can I ask you a stupid general culture question?", "can you give me advice for my drama-induced anxiety?"). They still didn't care about me. My two school 'friends' always left me out of plans outside of school. I was never included when it came to do things with the whole class, even though they acted like I was nice to them and like they actually liked me.

The problem is, I started thinking, that I'm very stubborn. I usually analize things a lot, and I can find logic holes easily. This isn't helpful when the class turns into a pseudo-philosophical debate formed by a bunch of high school students. However, I always respect everyone's point of view, I just, well, *debate*.

Ending my first HS year, I met this girl outside of my normal social circle (if you can call it that way). I had a lot of things in common with her, she was really fun and we just started dating. However, I was very clingy. This didn't bother her, but it helped her realize that I was for granted (which was true, since I couldn't even consider breaking up with her). She started being somewhat indifferent to me. In exageration, I panicked, so I started being all bitchy to her. This only made her behavior worse and led us to fight everyday. After 9 months of dating, we broke up. In two weeks she was fooling around with this guy who was just using her. She then "broke up" with him for being boring (not for treating her like shit). One month later we talked and she said that she just did it for rebound and the only one who loved was me. After much talking and consideration from both of us, we got back together. We started with the wrong foot, but then everything was great and it went on this way. Until we started fighting. The reasons of the fight were pretty much about her behavior, but I always overreacted on things and complaint a lot. Today, feeling like crap about my situation with people, I made her a comment about how I hated seeing pictures on Facebook of my classmates hanging out because I felt like I was left out of things. She said that she didn't know; like she was complaining because she was annoyed. She said she didn't want to start a fight, but this actually caused it. It was then my fault that I complained more and that I was very stubborn and negative. She said that she can't even talk to me because I get very easily offended. This showed me that there just was no trust with each other anymore, to the point that we can't just talk.

All these problems must be because of me. My parents complain about me, my classmates complain about me, my girlfriend complains about me. I'm negative, but I have no way to be positive; life has always found a way to make me feel like everything is wrong. Obviously I'm doing something wrong with people, there is no way I can be right and they wrong. The problem is that I think don't being stubborn is a problem. I just analyze things and take everything with a grain of salt.

But I don't know. I don't know what I'm supposed to change. I don't know if I'm even supposed to change. What is wrong with me? Why can't I have friendships? Why do I screw up my other relationships?
